habitat.name: Yellowstone River Valley
habitat.climate: Semi-arid with cold winters and warm summers
habitat.description: A vibrant river valley featuring winding waterways, grassy meadows, and stands of cottonwood trees supporting a complex web of wildlife.

organisms.imagePrompt: lush green bunchgrass growing in rich soil
organisms.description: A hardy perennial grass that captures sunlight to produce energy through photosynthesis.
adaptations: Deep root systems to survive dry spells

organisms.imagePrompt: large brown elk grazing in a sunny meadow
organisms.description: A large herbivore that travels in herds and feeds extensively on grasses and shrubs.
adaptations: Flat teeth specialized for grinding tough plant material
Herd behavior for protection against predators

organisms.imagePrompt: beaver gnawing on a tree branch near water
organisms.description: A semi-aquatic rodent that feeds on inner tree bark and aquatic plants while engineering wetland habitats.
adaptations: Strong front incisors to cut down trees
Webbed hind feet for efficient swimming

organisms.imagePrompt: gray wolf standing alert in a grassy clearing
organisms.description: An apex predator that hunts in packs to regulate herbivore populations.
adaptations: Strong jaws and sharp canine teeth

organisms.imagePrompt: majestic bald eagle perched high on a dead tree branch
organisms.description: A powerful bird of prey that feeds primarily on fish and small mammals.
adaptations: Incredible eyesight to spot prey from great heights
Hooked beak and sharp talons for grasping

organisms.imagePrompt: shelf fungi growing on the side of a decaying log
organisms.description: Wood-decaying organisms that break down dead organic matter and return nutrients to the soil.
adaptations: Enzymes that dissolve tough plant lignin and cellulose
Spore dispersal mechanisms for wide distribution

relationships.description: Elk consume the blue grama grass to obtain energy and nutrients.
Beavers eat wetland grasses and herbaceous plants alongside tree bark.
Gray wolves hunt and consume elk to sustain their pack.
Wolves occasionally prey upon beavers when other food sources are scarce.
Elk and beavers compete for access to riparian woody plants and shoreline vegetation.

environmentalFeatures.name: Winding River
environmentalFeatures.description: A cool flowing water channel that provides hydration and aquatic habitats.

environmentalFeatures.name: Sunlit Meadow
environmentalFeatures.description: An open expanse of nutrient-rich soil and abundant sunlight supporting plant growth.

challenges.prompt: Identify the evidence demonstrating that wolves help maintain a healthy plant community.
challenges.explanation: Gray wolves prey on herbivores like elk, preventing overgrazing and allowing riverside plants and grasses to recover and thrive.

evidenceChoices.text: Wolves howl loudly during moonlit nights in the valley.
When wolf packs are present, herbivore overgrazing drops and streamside vegetation flourishes.
Wolves have thick fur coats that protect them from winter snowstorms.

challenges.prompt: Select the observation proving that bracket fungi function as decomposers in this habitat.
challenges.explanation: Bracket fungi secrete specialized enzymes to break down tough dead wood, releasing essential nutrients back into the soil.

evidenceChoices.text: Bracket fungi grow exclusively on the shaded sides of living trees.
Brightly colored caps attract flying insects during summer months.
Fallen logs disappear faster over time as fungal threads dissolve woody tissue into soil nutrients.

challenges.prompt: Choose the piece of data supporting the claim that grasses form the foundation of the local food web.
challenges.explanation: Grasses perform photosynthesis to capture solar energy, providing the primary food source for all grazing herbivores in the ecosystem.

evidenceChoices.text: Stomach contents of multiple herbivores consist primarily of digested grass fibers and blades.
Grass roots hold loose soil particles tightly together during heavy rainstorms.
Blue grama blades turn golden brown when exposed to freezing autumn temperatures.

challenges.prompt: Identify the observation showing a competitive relationship between herbivores in the valley.
challenges.explanation: Elk and beavers overlap in their diet regarding riparian plants, leading to direct competition for limited food resources.

evidenceChoices.text: Beavers build complex dams using mud and fallen tree branches.
Elk and beavers feed on the exact same shoreline shrubs, resulting in reduced food availability for both.
Bald eagles soar above the river looking for swimming fish.

challenges.prompt: Select the evidence verifying that bald eagles occupy a high trophic level in the ecosystem.
challenges.explanation: As tertiary consumers, bald eagles feed on secondary consumers and fish, accumulating energy from multiple lower trophic levels.

evidenceChoices.text: Bald eagles build massive stick nests high in old-growth pine trees.
Young eaglets practice flapping their wings before taking their first flight.
Observations confirm that eagles capture fish and small mammals rather than feeding on plants.

disruptionScenario.event: A severe drought significantly reduces the growth of blue grama grass across the river valley.
cascadeEffects: Primary consumers like elk and beavers experience food shortages and declining populations.
Secondary consumers such as wolves have less prey available, leading to reduced pack sizes.
disruptionScenario.question: How does a shortage at the producer level ripple upward through the entire food chain?

data.intent: Use evidence to support a claim about an ecosystem
